text:
emily.s: FYI customer ACME reported p99 token latency up ~3x in eu-west-2 starting ~10:30 UTC. They sent traces showing heavy stall on token generation. Escalating.
ops-bot: Alert: high-p99-latency (eu-west-2). 24 nodes > p99 threshold. Link: https://observability.redwood/internal/alerts/5212349999 :rotating_light:
dan.k: Any rollout around that time? driver/kernel/firmware?
emily.s: We pushed CUDA 12.3 driver to eu-west-2 canary at 09:45 and rolled to remainder at 10:20. Correlates.
priya.n: Customers see heavy disk IO wait on host, KV-cache miss latencies spike in traces. Could be NVMe qdepth issues after driver change.
alex.l: Repro steps to confirm: run iostat and nvme top on a degraded node + run embedding load to simulate traffic. If QD spikes -> likely host-side IO interference.
jamal.r: I'm on-call for infra. I'll grab a node and run quick checks. Running:
```
ssh core@node-eu2-07
sudo iostat -x 1 10
sudo nvme list
sudo dmesg | tail -n 80
sudo nvidia-smi dmon -s u
```
emily.s: Also customer traces show KV cache flushes at hotspots. If driver changes altered NVMe scheduling, could exacerbate kernel pagecache interactions.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout eu-west-2 CUDA 12.3 completed at 10:20 by ci:driver-release #428
dan.k: If we can repro locally, try reverting one node to previous driver (12.2) and compare p99. Also check host kernel patches pushed last week (we did a backport to 5.10.x on these hosts).
priya.n: I already checked kernel: backport was in the control plane at 08:50 but not rolled to all hosts until 09:50 — overlap with driver rollout.
alex.l: Immediate mitigations: 1) divert traffic off suspect nodes (cordon + drain) 2) roll back driver on a small set 3) enable cgroup blkio limits to protect NVMe from cold cache flush storms.
jamal.r: Cordoning two nodes now and migrating pods -> `kubectl cordon node-eu2-07 && kubectl drain node-eu2-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
jamal.r: Quick iostat sample:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await
nvme0n1          120.00  95.00  9600   7600     16.7      3.8     32.1
```
jamal.r: avgqu-sz 3.8, await 32ms under load. Not massive but spikes to 250-400ms intermittently.
dan.k: Can you capture `perf record -a -g -o /tmp/perf.data  sleep 30` during a spike and share? Also `echo 2 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` on a repro node to see cache effect (careful).
priya.n: We tried `drop_caches` on a canary node; p99 dropped ~40% for 5 minutes then climbed back. Suggests aggressive pagecache eviction with driver I/O pattern.
emily.s: Customer-facing note: told ACME we're investigating and will apply mitigation within 60m. They want ETA for rollback if needed.
alex.l: Proposal: do a targeted rollback of CUDA driver on 3 nodes, and enable IO prioritization via blkio cgroup for caching daemon. If rollback reduces p99, widen rollback.
jamal.r: Starting targeted rollback on node-eu2-07: `dpkg -i /opt/drivers/nvidia-12.2.deb && systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` will run now.
support-bot: ACME support ticket #8765 updated: "We see improvement on some requests, still noisy" — customer posted new trace.
jamal.r: After rollback, sampling iostat shows awaits back to 10-20ms baseline. KV-cache hit latency p99 dropped ~55% on that node. Early win.
dan.k: Good. Next steps: bisect whether kernel backport or driver combo is root. Run controlled matrix: (driver12.2/12.3) x (kernel old/new) on 2x2 nodes.
priya.n: I'll provision repro matrix in lab and run synthetic traffic (embedding + chat) with our perf harness. Also adding fio stress to simulate background IO.
emily.s: For immediate cluster mitigation, continue cordon/drain of rolling nodes still on 12.3 and route traffic to healthy nodes in other regions. Ops to prep rollback plan if matrix points to driver.
jamal.r: I'll keep rolling rollback until we confirm. Notifying infra leads. /cc @alex.l @priya.n 
ops-bot: Incident timeline updated. Notes will be compiled into postmortem after stabilization.
emily.s: Thanks all — keep updates short here. I'll update ACME in 20m.
